description: UTAH DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES (DHHS) PROPOSAL FOR ACTIVITIES WITHIN THE STRENGTHENING U.S. PUBLIC HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE, WORKFORCE, AND DATA SYSTEMS GRANT. - THE UTAH DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES (DHHS) SERVES MANY FUNCTIONS, FROM JUVENILE JUSTICE TO CHRONIC DISEASE. THERE ARE MANY AREAS FOR ALIGNMENT AND IMPROVEMENT WITHIN THE PUBLIC HEALTH SYSTEM. DHHS HAS NOT HAD THE CAPACITY TO CONDUCT COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENTS RELATED TO WORKFORCE IN THE RECENT PAST. THIS GRANT PROVIDES AN OPPORTUNITY TO ASSESS THE CURRENT PUBLIC HEALTH SYSTEM IN UTAH AND DEVELOP PLANS TO IMPROVE THE DELIVERY OF SERVICES TO THE RESIDENTS OF UTAH THROUGH BETTER STAFFING PRACTICES, STRENGTHENED FOUNDATIONS OF PUBLIC HEALTH, AND MODERNIZED DATA SYSTEMS.  DHHS'S GOAL FOR THE NEXT 5 YEARS IS TO STRENGTHEN WORKFORCE, FOUNDATIONAL CAPABILITIES, AND DATA MODERNIZATION IN EACH STRATEGY LISTED IN THE GRANT.  A1 WORKFORCE: HIRING DEDICATED STAFF WITHIN THE PUBLIC HEALTH SYSTEM TO FURTHER GOALS OF THE GRANT, INCLUDING WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT SUPPORT STAFF, A DATA MODERNIZATION DIRECTOR AND SUPPORT COORDINATION STAFF, AND STAFF WITHIN THE SYSTEM (SUPPORTING LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENTS AND OTHER PARTNERS); CONDUCTING NEEDS ASSESSMENTS TO LEARN ABOUT WORKFORCE NEEDS, IDENTIFY TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES, AND EXPLORE EXPERIENCES OF WORKPLACE CULTURE, AS WELL AS TO ASSESS RESPONSE TRAINING NEEDS AND DATA SYSTEM CAPACITY, GAPS, AND OPPORTUNITIES; BUILDING BETTER PUBLIC HEALTH RECRUITMENT SYSTEMS AND OFFERING HIRING INCENTIVES.  A2: FOUNDATIONAL CAPABILITIES: DEVELOPING PLANS AND AGREEMENTS WITH PARTNERS TO HELP TRAIN AND PROVIDE ADDITIONAL STAFF IN THE EVENT OF FUTURE PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCIES; IMPROVING EXISTING HEALTH COMMUNICATION STRATEGIES TO MORE EFFECTIVELY PROVIDE HEALTH INFORMATION TO DIVERSE POPULATIONS ACROSS THE STATE; ENHANCING ORGANIZATIONAL COMPETENCIES WITH A FOCUS ON EQUITY.  A3: DATA MODERNIZATION: DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING PLANS FOR PUBLIC HEALTH DATA MODERNIZATION, INCLUDING POSSIBLE IMPLEMENTATION OF A COMMON ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD PLATFORM TO BE USED BY PUBLIC HEALTH AGENCIES ACROSS THE STATE AND REPLACING CURRENT SYSTEMS FOR COMMUNICABLE DISEASE REPORTING; AND CREATING A CURRENT DATA MANAGEMENT PLAN, WITH GUIDANCE FROM CDC, TO BE UPDATED AS NEW INFORMATION BECOMES AVAILABLE.

cfda_info.cfda_objectives: The purpose of the Emerging Infections Programs (EIP) is to assist in local, state, and national efforts to prevent, control, and monitor the public health impact of infectious diseases. The EIP cooperative agreement was formed in 1995 as a key component of CDC’s national strategy to address and reduce emerging infectious disease (EID) threats.  The EIP is a population-based network of state health agencies and their collaborators, including (but not limited to) academic institutions, local health departments, public health and clinical laboratories, infection control professionals, and healthcare providers.   The unique strength of the EIP lies in the network’s ability to quickly translate surveillance and research activities into informed policy and public health practice.

cfda_info.cfda_objectives: The intent of this program is to fund state, local, and territorial public health departments for HHS Secretarial declared and non-declared public health emergencies having an overwhelming impact on jurisdictional resources. These emergencies require federal support to effectively respond to, manage, and address a significant public health threat. CDC seeks to enhance the Nation’s ability to rapidly mobilize and respond to specific public health crises or emergencies. In addition to immediate response activities, this program provides a mechanism to accelerate readiness for an impending infectious disease threat or other public health crises identified on the event horizon.
